answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates urgency, but exp_73 explicitly warns that targeted discounting acquires cohorts with -12% retention and non-renewal. Chasing this with promotional_pricing repeats a known failure pattern at scale. Instead, activate the at-risk SMB base through product engagement. memory_91 shows activation messaging improved week-one engagement; combined with memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifts adoption) and memory_31 (signup simplification drives activation), a coordinated activation campaign can deepen product value perception and reduce price sensitivity among existing customers. This addresses churn directly without acquiring low-quality cohorts. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but don't address immediate churn. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB crisis. A standard experiment on activation messaging for at-risk SMB accounts preserves the option to escalate to pricing if engagement gains prove insufficient, while avoiding the retention cliff documented in exp_73.
